A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DDPD research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material that was relocated or renumbered.

before.justification: v1 reports original text8, OpenWebText, and ImageNet generation experiments, with numerical comparisons, ablations, and generated examples in Section 6 and Appendices E–F.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and adds empirical sampling-convergence diagnostics and ImageNet evaluations with classifier-free guidance and additional temperature settings.

M1.justification: The planner–denoiser decomposition, adaptive Gillespie sampler, time correction, pretrained mask-denoiser reuse, and training objectives remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the implementation listings are retained; the new experiments explore settings of the existing framework.

E1.justification: Both versions use text8 character generation, OpenWebText language modeling, and ImageNet 256 × 256 token generation. The added convergence and guidance experiments retain these datasets and task requirements.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain DFM and autoregressive models on text8, SEDD and GPT-2 on OpenWebText, and mask diffusion and MaskGIT on ImageNet. The new guidance and temperature comparisons use existing methods; their changed configurations belong to evaluation settings.

E3.justification: Figure 2 revises reported text8 sampling budgets from 250–1000 to 256–1024 steps. New experiments monitor convergence at corruption-probability thresholds of 0.05 and 0.01 and evaluate CFG scale 2.0 and additional temperature schedules, including initialization at 3.0. These are targeted protocol extensions; existing training settings remain unchanged, and the budget revision does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's existing model-quality, sampler-component, and refinement ablations, v2 adds convergence diagnostics for remaining noise, changing noise labels, and stopping behavior (Appendix E.2, Figure 8). Appendix E.4.1 also investigates guidance–temperature interactions and tuned sampling heuristics, substantially extending analysis of convergence and sensitivity.

E5.justification: The new Figure 8 displays error bars on average remaining-noise curves, adding uncertainty reporting absent from v1's plots. Their meaning and calculation are unspecified, and no repeated-run counts or seeds are supplied; additional repetitions cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: Existing numerical tables are retained, but v2 adds convergence findings and guidance/tuning results that materially qualify comparative performance. At 16 steps, new Table 11 reports MaskGIT versus DDPD FID of 2.48 versus 7.93 and Inception Scores of 284.20 versus 359.69. These settings were absent from v1. Figure 2's middle curves also change alongside revised sampling budgets, precluding a same-setting performance comparison.

T1.justification: The decomposition propositions, self-loop CTMC argument, mask-denoiser marginalization, Theorem 4.1, and proofs and derivations in Appendices A–C are retained. The added convergence evidence is empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about planning and denoising, adaptive error correction, ELBO-based training, and improved text and image generation. The main contributions are not redefined.

C2.justification: Appendix E.4.1 extends the quality–diversity interpretation to CFG and high-temperature sampling. It explains why heuristics tuned for mask diffusion do not transfer directly to DDPD: the planner identifies atypical initial tokens as noisy and corrects them, potentially improving quality while reducing diversity. This adds a focused applicability qualification to v1's discussion.

D1.justification: Section 8 newly reports model-checkpoint access alongside the code already linked in v1, and the added experiments document guidance and temperature parameters. Conversely, the shortened image-generation discussion omits v1's full temperature-sweep list and explicit half-parallel, half-refinement allocation. Appendix D's architecture, training, hardware, and pseudocode details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chen, Zhang, and Hinton's Analog Bits citation to the self-correction discussion and expands discussion of sampling heuristics from the already cited Yu et al. work. The broader positioning relative to discrete diffusion and flow methods remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 reorganizes the introductory advantages into numbered points, edits the time-correction explanation, and compresses the ImageNet discussion. Reproducibility and ethics statements move from Appendices G–H to Sections 8–9, and the publication header changes. Most prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the four-panel convergence Figure 8 and Tables 10–11, revises Figure 2's middle plot and legend, and adjusts figure placement and numbering. It also corrects the MaskGIT temperature label in v1 Figure 13(c), now Figure 14(c), to 0.6. Existing generation images and most plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The added convergence diagnostics and guided, tuned ImageNet comparisons improve empirical transparency, including revealing settings where MaskGIT achieves better FID than DDPD. They provide useful checks on stopping behavior and the scope of comparative advantages. The gain is limited by undefined error bars and the removal of some sampling details; the core method, theory, and most evidence remain unchanged.
